reviewer_statement: Developer native-language source-semantic review against frozen Python 1.2. Exact source mathematical behavior, deterministic reference channel mapping, NumPy float64 standard container conversion, finite/nonfinite source domain, empty-axis and one-channel numerical results, and native error equivalents are pinned by six distinct SHA256 test records. This is not independent certification, live Python ndarray identity, arbitrary Python user-defined coercion protocols or CRAN release approval.
native_language_semantic_policy: R double arrays are the numerical native representations of NumPy float64 3D ndarrays; native R conditions stand for source errors. An explicit python_boundary_mode selects the source domain without changing finite-only ordinary R behavior. The Python keyword-only binder, Python object subclass/array protocols and warning class identity cannot be identical in the native R language.

case_evidence.description: Required 3D ALR array, reference index, integer n_dimensions shape and native source-boundary mode.
Positive, negative and extreme logits in float64 numeric/Boolean/decimal-string and complex 3D arrays; standard nested scalar containers and empty axes.
Inverse exp(z) direct reference-channel insertion and sum-normalization over k=1,2,3,5,7 including source Inf/NaN overflow patterns.
Reject bad 3D shape, wrong k-1 channel width, invalid Python shape/index arguments and unsupported dtype leaves.
Numeric 3D native R array of (curve,time,K) with reference channel, zero axes and exact normalized source values.
Inverse additive log-ratio transform via direct exponentiation and reference logit zero, without stable-logsumexp replacement.

known_language_specific_limits: Native R arrays are not Python ndarray objects
Arbitrary Python extension objects and Python keyword-only calling syntax are not native R protocols
Native R warnings and error conditions are not Python NumPy warnings/ValueErrors
